newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sets T-bill plans for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia sets T-bill plans for 1997.

text.p: Russia plans to issue 259.0 trillion roubles of GKO discount Treasury bills and 74.0 trillion roubles of OFZ interest bearing government bonds in 1997, according to a copy of the draft 1997 budget obtained by Reuters on Tuesday.
In 1997 Russia will repay 244.0 trillion roubles of GKO T-bills, and repay 44.3 trillion roubles of OFZ bonds, including interest payments, the budget draft said.
As a result GKO issues will raise 15.0 trillion roubles and OFZ bond issues will raise 29.7 trillion roubles for the government in 1997, it said.
This will cover 92 percent of domestic borrowing to cover the deficit, said the draft, prepared on August 22.
The draft put the 1997 deficit at 89.1 trillion roubles or 3.3 percent of gross domestic product.
A revised draft submitted to parliament on Monday put the deficit at 90.7 trillion roubles, but still 3.3 percent of GDP.
The August 22 draft said 48.5 trillion roubles of the deficit would be covered by domestic borrowing and 40.6 trillion by external borrowing.

Apart from issuing T-bills and OFZ bonds, the government plans next year to issue 10.0 trillion roubles of OGSZ savings bonds, and repay 7.0 trillion roubles of savings bonds issued in 1996, raising a net 3.0 trillion roubles, it said.

It will also issue 1.0 trillion roubles in gold-backed bonds, and 5.0 trillion roubles in a new short-term instrument known as non-market bonds, which will not trade in a secondary market, the draft said.

As of August 30 the nominal value of outstanding government securities was 188.17 trillion roubles, with a market value of 163.65 trillion. The market value of GKO T-bills was 142.08 trillion and of OFZ bonds was 20.78 trillion.
